cl_gen_deaths_level_changes.q: Can drug levels change after death?
cl_gen_deaths_level_changes.short: Yes. Levels can rise or fall and differ between blood vessels.
cl_gen_deaths_level_changes.but: These studies cannot predict the change in one ordinary death.
how: Four selected overdose deaths showed large differences between blood vessels. A medicine given in hospital varied less.
In one person, all imipramine samples after death were about 2 to 8 times the earlier hospital level.
A collection of published reports and Finnish records found that the gap between body samples differs by drug.
Repeated tests found rises for some drugs and falls for others. The first sample was often taken hours after death.

cl_gen_deaths_level_cause.q: Can a blood level show that a drug caused death?
cl_gen_deaths_level_cause.short: Not on its own. Levels overlap between deaths with different causes.
cl_gen_deaths_level_cause.but: The rules and tests used to decide the cause also affect the comparison.
how: In an English autopsy study, MDMA levels in drug deaths overlapped with levels in injury deaths.
An older review reports a similar overlap for morphine. It also cites comparisons with people who survived an overdose.
Finnish data compare blood after death with treatment ranges, not the same people before and after death.
At one US centre, full autopsy changed suspected drug-death classifications in both directions. This study tested drug presence, not levels.

cl_can_deaths_attributed.q: Can cannabis cause a sudden death?
cl_can_deaths_attributed.short: These studies do not settle that question.
cl_can_deaths_attributed.but: The linked deaths are selected reports with no comparison group.
how: A review collected 13 deaths linked to recent use. Eight had significant heart disease or other illness; five lacked a blood test showing recent use.
Larger studies, relayed by the review, point both ways. Some found no increase in deaths.
A Finnish table prints 0% as poisonings mainly attributed to THC, rounded to whole percent. That does not prove an exact zero count.
The reviewers encourage counting cannabis as a contributor in appropriate cases, but give no estimate of missed deaths.
